A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same layer-pruning study. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures support comparison, including matching material relocated or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original pruning experiments across seven language models, including MMLU and BoolQ accuracy, C4 loss, representation similarities, and hyperparameter ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains these experiments and adds original CoT-MMLU, GSM8K, HellaSwag, and alternative pruning-strategy results.

M1.justification: Both versions retain angular-distance-based selection of contiguous layer blocks, removal followed by optional QLoRA healing, and the simpler deepest-layer pruning strategy. The new experiments do not revise the proposed procedures.

E1.justification: V2 Section 5 adds GSM8K mathematical reasoning and HellaSwag commonsense reasoning, substantially extending evaluation beyond the original MMLU, BoolQ, and C4 coverage. It also evaluates MMLU with chain-of-thought generation. Original training and evaluation datasets remain.

E2.justification: Appendix C.4 and Figure 11 add random-layer and shallow-layer pruning as actual comparators against similarity-informed pruning on Llama-2-7B. This is a focused addition; the existing simple deepest-layer and unpruned-model comparisons remain.

E3.justification: The added evaluations introduce CoT generation, GSM8K pass@1 with single-generation answer checking, and HellaSwag testing. Figure 11 specifies LoRA rank 64 for its new comparison. Original experimental settings remain, including the unresolved five-shot versus zero-shot MMLU inconsistency between the main text and appendix.

E4.justification: Section 5 adds experiments contrasting reasoning requirements with extended CoT generation as explanations for pruning sensitivity. Appendix C.4 additionally tests whether similarity-based layer selection outperforms random or shallow deletion. These substantially extend the analyses of applicability and layer selection; existing prompting, seed, and LoRA-rank ablations are retained.

E5.justification: The default seed-zero determinism statement and three-seed finetuning ablation are unchanged, with v1 Figure 8 becoming v2 Figure 9. No new repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are reported.

E6.justification: V2 Figure 6 adds immediate performance degradation with pruning on GSM8K and HellaSwag, contrasting with CoT-MMLU's relatively stable region before collapse. Figure 11 adds better pre-collapse MMLU performance for similarity-informed pruning than random or shallow pruning. The original nine figures retain their plotted results; the substantive change is new findings rather than improved scores in existing experiments.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8 retain the residual-network reasoning, angular-distance definition, block-selection objective, and suggested auxiliary healing loss. The new reasoning-versus-generation hypotheses are qualitative interpretations, not new formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: V2 retains the finding that substantial pruning preserves QA performance, but reframes the contribution around knowledge storage and adds a central claim that deeper layers support higher-level reasoning. The earlier broad downstream-performance and consumer-GPU efficiency framing is narrowed by explicitly acknowledging reasoning failures.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the new task contrast as initial evidence that deeper layers support reasoning rather than merely enabling long token generation. This introduces an important task-dependent limitation to pruning and develops a knowledge-versus-computation interpretation that v1 largely left for future investigation.

D1.justification: V2 specifies 40GB A100 capacity and supplies EleutherAI task identifiers and answer-checking details for the new evaluations. It removes v1's illustrative memory/FLOP calculation. Model repository paths, data-loading instructions, libraries, and core healing hyperparameter tables are retained.

R1.justification: The extensive original literature review is largely retained in Appendix A. V2 expands the already-cited ShortGPT overlap into a substantive comparison, adds references supporting the new benchmarks, evaluation procedures, and LayerSkip discussion, and removes several broad scaling-law and quantization background citations.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially recast, the full literature review moves to Appendix A with a short main-text replacement, and the discussion is reorganized around competing scientific hypotheses. Existing experimental appendices become B and C, alongside document-wide citation-style and heading changes.

P2.justification: V2 adds the three-panel task comparison in Figure 6 and pruning-baseline Figure 11 while retaining all original figures and tables. It corrects Figure 1's healing-color caption, enlarges the seed-ablation plot, and applies conference formatting with repositioned displays. Original appendix Figures 6–9 become Figures 7–10.

improvement.justification: V1 left task dependence largely as future work. V2 Figure 6 supplies an important applicability boundary: reasoning can deteriorate immediately even when QA remains robust, while CoT-MMLU tests an alternative explanation involving generation length. Figure 11 strengthens the evidence for layer selection. These additions substantially improve the support and qualification of the central conclusions, although the new task evidence covers only Llama-2-70B and does not establish the proposed mechanism conclusively.
